hints.title: Sequential Allotment
hints.text: Distribute 1, 2, 3, ... candies sequentially, wrapping around the people array using modulo operations.

hints.title: Bounded Step Total
hints.text: The total number of distributions is bounded by the square root of 2 times candies, which is at most about 45000 iterations.

hints.title: Remaining Inventory Assignment
hints.text: At each step, grant the minimum of the requested candy count and the remaining inventory to the current recipient.

hints.title: See the blueprint
hints.text:
```python
class Solution:
    def distributeCandies(self, candies: int, num_people: int) -> list[int]:
        res = [0] * num_people
        give = 1
        idx = 0
        while candies > 0:
            amount = min(candies, give)
            res[idx % num_people] += amount
            candies -= amount
            give += 1
            idx += 1
        return res
```

complexity.whyNaiveFails: Direct simulation is already optimal because the sum of 1..k candies scales quadratically, terminating in O(sqrt(C)) steps.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Simulating sequential delivery directly within the output array takes only O(N) space.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Candidate should understand the arithmetic series bound and implement clean round-robin array indexing.
complexity.notes: Final recipient receives whatever candies remain, even if fewer than the step amount.
